_about: Claims deleted from records because they are impossible, not merely unsourced (Nathan, 3 October 2026: 'Anything in that category should be deleted rather than withheld, with a note saying what it claimed and why it is impossible, so nobody restores it later'). check_removed_claims.php fails if any of these sentences is found in a record again; the WordPress file (inventory/wp_content.json) still holds them as they arrived. removedRecords lists person records removed because they do not belong in the archive; the check fails if a live person record by that name returns.

claims.title: Father Francisco Garcés
claims.claim: He was beatified by Pope John Paul II on September 22, 1787.
claims.why: Garcés died in 1781, six years before the date it gives (Jerry Reynolds, article #839, gives his dates as 1738–1781), and John Paul II was born in 1920.

removedRecords.title: John Wayne
removedRecords.why: He filmed here (Placerita Canyon, Beale's Cut, Hoot Gibson's rodeo near Bouquet Junction): a location credit, not a connection to the valley. A person belongs for what they did here.
removedRecords.by: scripts/import/remove_john_wayne.php; the review decision and name canon are marked external so a rerun does not rebuild him

removedRecords.title: Juan José Francisco de Gracia ("Chico") Lopez
removedRecords.why: Jerry Reynolds's name for the gold discoverer, which joins three men: the discoverer's uncle (Juan José Francisco), the discoverer (José Francisco de Gracia) and his cousin Francisco "Chico" López. A record standing for two people is worse than none. The discoverer is #18834; Chico has his own record.

removedRecords.title: Juan Bandini
removedRecords.why: A San Diego ranchero whose tie to the valley ran through his son-in-law, Cave Couts, whose 1849 drive with Bandini's cattle went by the coast. His tie is his son-in-law's, not his own (Nathan, 3 October 2026).

removedRecords.title: José Antonio Aguirre
removedRecords.why: A San Diego merchant who received the Tejon grant with Ygnacio del Valle in 1843. The Tejon is outside the valley (Nathan, 3 October 2026).

removedRecords.title: California Battalion
removedRecords.why: Folded into John C. Frémont (#307): no source here names a California Battalion; the sources tell of Frémont's "buckskin battalion", and his record holds it.

removedRecords.title: Catalonian Volunteers
removedRecords.why: Folded into the Portolá Expedition (#938): the Volunteers are in this archive as the expedition's soldiers under Pedro Fages.

removedRecords.title: De Anza Expedition
removedRecords.why: Retired: no source in the archive puts the expedition in the Santa Clarita Valley.
